cut: 2D v1 stills (22 Nov, en only). Owner, 22 Nov: 'More into ICEYE' then 'Combine 2 and 1' (the Gen5 satellite, 16 Nov, and the €2B bid for Avio, 17 Nov). A sequel to Sleep Tight (Helsinki 2). Device: a borrowed format, the company's own release notes.
argument: ICEYE, which began as a 2012 Aalto University course project, unveiled an 11-centimeter radar satellite and bid two billion euros for an Italian rocket maker in the same week; the deal still needs government approval.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word

text.en: ICEYE began / as an Aalto / course [project].

captions.source: Aalto University: 'ICEYE was founded as a course project at Aalto University in 2012' (aalto.fi; as used in Sleep Tight, plan 9 Nov).

text.en: 16 Nov: / a radar satellite / that sees [11 cm].

captions.source: ICEYE press release, 16 Nov 2026: Gen5 SAR satellite, resolution 11 cm for government customers and 16 cm for commercial, an onboard AI processor; first units in customer service in 2027 (Janes; SatNews 16 Nov; Via Satellite 16 Nov). Search summaries, 22 Nov.

text.en: 17 Nov: / a bid for an / Italian / [rocket maker].

captions.source: Defense News and Via Satellite, 17 Nov 2026: an ICEYE subsidiary, Iris 2 S.p.A., made an all-cash offer to take Avio private at €41 a share. Search summaries, 22 Nov.
The offer values Avio at €2 billion ($2.2 billion) (Defense News, 17 Nov 2026).
An Avio spokesman told Defense News that US government approval would be required in the event of a takeover by ICEYE, as well as Italian government approval (17 Nov 2026). The bid is pending.

v2s.en: 11 cm for governments, 16 cm commercial · in service from 2027

v3s.en: All cash, €41 a share, via a subsidiary

post.en: ICEYE began as a 2012 Aalto course project. On 16 Nov it unveiled a radar satellite that sees 11 cm. On 17 Nov it bid €2 billion for Avio, an Italian rocket maker. The deal still needs Rome's and Washington's OK.
